items.title: Finite periodic Haar transform

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 3 and 7
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement:
Let $J\ge1$, $N=2^J$, and $x\in\mathbb R^N$, with the Euclidean inner product and norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Put $a^{(0)}=x$. For $r=1,\ldots,J$ and $0\le k<2^{J-r}$ define
$$a^{(r)}_k=\frac{a^{(r-1)}_{2k}+a^{(r-1)}_{2k+1}}{\sqrt2},\qquad d^{(r)}_k=\frac{a^{(r-1)}_{2k}-a^{(r-1)}_{2k+1}}{\sqrt2}.$$
The finite periodic Haar transform $T_Hx$ is the length-$N$ vector obtained by listing $a^{(J)}_0$, then $d^{(J)}_0$, then the entries of $d^{(J-1)}$, and continuing through $d^{(1)}$. The input is already of even dyadic length; this convention uses no padding and no endpoint extension.

items.title: Periodic finite orthogonal compact-filter wavelet transform

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 3 and 7
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement:
Let $L\ge1$, let $N$ be even with $N\ge2L$, and let $h=(h_0,\ldots,h_{L-1})\in\mathbb R^L$. Set $g_j=(-1)^j h_{L-1-j}$ for $0\le j<L$, and set $h_j=g_j=0$ for all other integers $j$. The pair $(h,g)$ is an admissible orthogonal filter pair when
$$\sum_jh_j=\sqrt2,\quad \sum_jg_j=0,\quad \sum_jh_jh_{j-2r}=\delta_{r0},\quad \sum_jg_jg_{j-2r}=\delta_{r0},\quad \sum_jh_jg_{j-2r}=0\quad(r\in\mathbb Z).$$
Here $\delta_{r0}=1$ for $r=0$ and $0$ for $r\ne0$.
For $x\in\mathbb R^N$, define
$$a_k=\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}h_jx_{(2k+j)\bmod N},\qquad d_k=\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}g_jx_{(2k+j)\bmod N}\qquad(0\le k<N/2).$$
This is the one-level periodic analysis map. It has no padding: the indices are reduced modulo $N$. Its matrix $W$ has the $N/2$ rows for $a_k$ followed by the $N/2$ rows for $d_k$. Synthesis is, by definition, multiplication by $W^T$. A multilevel transform repeats this one-level rule on the approximation vector while its current length $M$ is even and $M\ge2L$, then stops; the boundary convention at every level is periodic modulo that level's current length.

items.title: Explicit four-tap Daubechies filter and its high-pass partner

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 8
Jelena Kovačević, Vivek K. Goyal, and Martin Vetterli, Fourier and Wavelet Signal Processing

items.statement:
Set
$$h=\frac1{4\sqrt2}(1+\sqrt3,\ 3+\sqrt3,\ 3-\sqrt3,\ 1-\sqrt3),\qquad g_j=(-1)^jh_{3-j}\quad(0\le j\le3).$$
Both filters are zero outside the indices $0,1,2,3$. The high-pass filter is therefore $g=(h_3,-h_2,h_1,-h_0)$. The exact admissibility and two-moment properties of this pair are the statement of [[thm-na-daubechies-d4-filter-qmf-and-two-moments]].

items.title: Smooth functions on the unit interval with bounded derivative data

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 13
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement: Let $q\ge1$ be an integer and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $[0,1]$. A real function $f:U\to\mathbb R$ belongs to the smooth derivative-bound class $\mathcal S^q$ when it is $C^q$ on $U$ in the sense of [[def-continuity-and-derivative-on-real-interval]]. For $0\le r\le q$ define $M_r(f)=\sup_{0\le t\le1}|f^{(r)}(t)|$, with $f^{(0)}=f$. These derivative bounds are finite because the derivatives are continuous on the compact interval. They are bounds on the restriction to $[0,1]$, not a norm on arbitrary extensions to $U$; no claim that this class exhausts $W^{q,\infty}(0,1)$ is part of the definition.

items.title: Haar cell-average projection on the unit interval

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 3
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement:
For an integer $J\ge0$, put $h=2^{-J}$ and $I_{J,k}=[kh,(k+1)h]$ for $0\le k<2^J$. For an integrable real function $f$ on $[0,1]$, its Haar cell-average projection is the piecewise constant function
$$P_Jf(x)=\frac1h\int_{I_{J,k}}f(t)\,dt\quad\text{when }x\in[kh,(k+1)h).$$
The value at $x=1$ is defined by the average on the last cell. The half-open intervals give an unambiguous partition for point values; changing endpoint values does not change the integrals or the $L^2$ error.

items.title: Hard m-term retention and soft thresholding of finite coefficients

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 15

items.statement:
Let $c\in\mathbb R^N$. For $m\in\{0,\ldots,N\}$, choose any set $S_m$ of $m$ indices whose absolute coefficients are among the $m$ largest, resolving ties arbitrarily. The hard m-term retention $H_m(c)$ has coordinate $c_i$ for $i\in S_m$ and $0$ otherwise. For a threshold $\lambda\ge0$, the soft-threshold vector $S_\lambda(c)$ has coordinates
$$S_\lambda(c)_i=\operatorname{sign}(c_i)(|c_i|-\lambda)_+,\qquad (t)_+=\max(t,0),$$
with $\operatorname{sign}(0)=0$. Soft thresholding shrinks retained coefficients; it is not defined by a prescribed number of retained terms.

items.title: Finite wavelet-coefficient Besov quasi-norm on a dyadic multilevel transform

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9, §9.2.3
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 13

items.statement:
For an integer $J\ge3$, a coarse block $a=(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)$, a real $s>0$, and $p>0$, define the finite wavelet-coefficient Besov quasi-norm
$$\|(a,d)\|_{b^s_{p,p}(J)}^p=\sum_{\nu=0}^3|a_\nu|^p+\sum_{j=2}^{J-1}2^{jp(s+1/2-1/p)}\sum_{k=0}^{2^j-1}|d_{j,k}|^p.$$
This is the wavelet coefficient convention, with one coarse block and detail blocks indexed by their number $2^j$ of coefficients. At the critical relation $p=(s+1/2)^{-1}$, every scale weight equals $1$, so the quasi-norm is exactly the $\ell^p$ quasi-norm of the full coefficient vector. This finite coefficient definition does not assert equivalence with an intrinsic function-space Besov norm.

items.title: Finite Riesz synthesis matrix and biorthogonal coefficient coordinates

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 11

items.statement:
Let $V\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ be invertible and suppose there are constants $0<A\le B<\infty$ such that
$$A\|z\|_2^2\le\|Vz\|_2^2\le B\|z\|_2^2\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb R^N.$$
Call $V$ a finite Riesz synthesis matrix and call $A,B$ Riesz bounds. For a signal $x\in\mathbb R^N$, the analysis coefficients are $c=V^{-1}x$ and synthesis is $x=Vc$. The inverse analysis matrix and synthesis matrix form a biorthogonal coordinate pair; unless $A=B=1$, coefficient truncation errors need not equal Euclidean tail energy.

items.title: Orthogonality, inverse, and Parseval identity for the finite periodic Haar transform

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 3 and 7
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement: For every $J\ge1$ and $x\in\mathbb R^{2^J}$, the transform $T_H$ of [[def-na-finite-periodic-haar-transform]] is an orthogonal linear map. Its inverse is $T_H^{T}$ and $\|T_Hx\|_2^2=\|x\|_2^2$.

items.title: Inverse and Parseval identity for a periodic orthogonal compact-filter transform

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 3 and 7
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement: For every admissible pair $(h,g)$, every even $N\ge2L$, and every $x\in\mathbb R^N$, the analysis matrix $W$ in [[def-na-periodic-orthogonal-compact-filter-dwt]] is orthogonal. Thus synthesis $W^T$ is its inverse and $\|Wx\|_2^2=\|x\|_2^2$. Every multilevel transform defined there is also orthogonal, with inverse given by reversing the stages and applying each stage's transpose.

items.title: The explicit four-tap Daubechies pair satisfies the orthogonal filter and two-moment conditions

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 8
Jelena Kovačević, Vivek K. Goyal, and Martin Vetterli, Fourier and Wavelet Signal Processing

items.statement: The pair $(h,g)$ in [[def-na-daubechies-d4-filter]] is admissible in [[def-na-periodic-orthogonal-compact-filter-dwt]]. In addition, $\sum_{j=0}^3j^rg_j=0$ for $r=0,1$, so the high-pass filter annihilates constant and affine data.

items.title: Haar cell averages approximate smooth bounded-derivative data at first order

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 3 and 9
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement:
Let $f\in\mathcal S^1$ with $M_1=M_1(f)$. For every integer $J\ge0$, with $h=2^{-J}$ and $P_J$ as in [[def-na-haar-cell-average-projection]],
$$\left(\int_0^1|f(x)-P_Jf(x)|^2\,dx\right)^{1/2}\le \frac{h}{\sqrt2}M_1.$$
Thus the cell-average Haar approximation has first-order error on the explicit derivative-bounded smooth class $\mathcal S^1$.

items.title: Hard m-term retention is optimal for an orthonormal coefficient basis

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 15

items.statement:
Let $U\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ satisfy $U^TU=UU^T=I_N$, let $x\in\mathbb R^N$, and set $c=Ux$. For any $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ let $P_Sc$ retain exactly the coordinates in $S$. Then
$$\|x-U^TP_Sc\|_2^2=\sum_{i\notin S}|c_i|^2.$$
Consequently, for every $0\le m\le N$, $H_m(c)$ from [[def-na-hard-soft-coefficient-thresholding]] minimizes reconstruction error over all choices retaining at most $m$ coefficients. Its squared error is exactly the sum of the discarded squared coefficients.

items.title: Biorthogonal coefficient truncation error is controlled by Riesz bounds

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 11

items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite Riesz synthesis matrix with bounds $A,B$ as in [[def-na-finite-riesz-synthesis-matrix]], let $c=V^{-1}x$, and retain coefficients in $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. Define $S^c=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\setminus S$, and define $(P_Sc)_i=c_i$ for $i\in S$ and $0$ otherwise. Then
$$A\sum_{i\notin S}|c_i|^2\le\|x-VP_Sc\|_2^2\le B\sum_{i\notin S}|c_i|^2.$$
Thus a biorthogonal transform has coefficient-tail error constants given by its Riesz bounds; an orthonormal identity with constant $1$ is the special case $A=B=1$.

items.title: Periodic multilevel transform using the four-tap Daubechies filter

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 8 and 15
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement: Let $J\ge3$ and $N=2^J$. Starting with $a^{(0)}=x\in\mathbb R^N$, for $\ell=1,\ldots,J-2$ apply one-level periodic analysis with the D4 pair of [[def-na-daubechies-d4-filter]] to the current approximation vector $a^{(\ell-1)}$, whose length is $N/2^{\ell-1}\ge8$. Store the detail vector $d^{(\ell)}$ and set the next approximation to $a^{(\ell)}$. Stop with the length-four vector $a^{(J-2)}$. The output consists of that coarse vector and all detail vectors, ordered from coarsest details to finest. At every stage indices are reduced modulo that stage's current length; there is no padding or symmetric extension.

items.title: Critical Besov coefficient control implies a best m-term squared-error rate

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9, §§9.2.2–9.2.3
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 15

items.statement:
Let $J\ge3$, $N=2^J$, $s>0$, and $p=(s+1/2)^{-1}\in(0,2)$. Let $U\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ be orthogonal, $x\in\mathbb R^N$, and $c=Ux$. Regard $c$ as one coarse block $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and detail blocks $d_j\in\mathbb R^{2^j}$ for $2\le j\le J-1$, with the norm of [[def-na-wavelet-coefficient-besov-quasinorm]]. For $1\le m\le N$, hard retention of the $m$ largest coefficients has reconstruction error
$$\|x-U^TH_m(c)\|_2\le \sqrt{\frac{p}{2-p}}\,\|c\|_{b^s_{p,p}(J)}\,m^{-s},$$
where $c=Ux$ and $U$ is the orthogonal analysis matrix.

items.title: Local support, affine cancellation, and normalization of multilevel D4 detail rows

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 7, 8 and 13
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement: In the multilevel transform of [[def-na-d4-periodic-multilevel-transform]], a detail row at stage $\ell$ has $2^{J-\ell}$ translates, is supported on at most $3(2^\ell-1)+1$ consecutive input indices on a periodic lift, has Euclidean norm $1$, and annihilates every affine function of the lifted sample index. Its $\ell^1$ norm, meaning the sum of absolute row entries, is at most the square root of its support size. Since $1\le\ell\le J-2$, this support has fewer than $N=2^J$ indices and so its lifted support contains no repeated residue modulo $N$.

items.title: Two D4 vanishing moments give a local coefficient bound for smooth periodic samples

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 13
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement:
Let $J\ge3$, $N=2^J$, and let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $1$-periodic and $C^2$. Its restriction to an open interval $U\supset[0,1]$ belongs to $\mathcal S^2$; write $M_2=M_2(f|_U)$. Form $x_n=N^{-1/2}f(n/N)$ for $0\le n<N$, and analyze $x$ with the multilevel D4 transform. For a detail coefficient $d_{j,k}$ at scale $j=J-\ell$ ($1\le\ell\le J-2$), one has
$$|d_{j,k}|\le\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}M_2\,2^{-5j/2}.$$

items.title: Smooth periodic samples have a best m-term D4 Besov-tail rate

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9, §9.2.3
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 8 and 13

items.statement:
Let $J\ge3$, $N=2^J$, and let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $1$-periodic and $C^2$, with $f|_U\in\mathcal S^2$ for an open interval $U\supset[0,1]$. Form the normalized sample vector $x_n=N^{-1/2}f(n/N)$ and its multilevel D4 coefficients $(a,d)$. For any $0<s<2$, set $p=(s+1/2)^{-1}$. Then
$$\|(a,d)\|_{b^s_{p,p}(J)}^p\le4M_0^p+\frac{(9\sqrt3M_2/2)^p\,2^{-2p(2-s)}}{1-2^{-p(2-s)}},$$
where $M_r=\sup_{[0,1]}|f^{(r)}|$, and for $1\le m\le N$,
$$\|x-U_N^TH_m(U_Nx)\|_2\le \sqrt{\frac p{2-p}}\left(4M_0^p+\frac{(9\sqrt3M_2/2)^p\,2^{-2p(2-s)}}{1-2^{-p(2-s)}}\right)^{1/p}m^{-s}.$$
The norm is the finite wavelet-coefficient convention of [[def-na-wavelet-coefficient-besov-quasinorm]]; no intrinsic Besov norm equivalence is asserted.

title: Wavelet transforms and nonlinear approximation — Examples

items.title: Periodic and symmetric padding give different Haar coefficients

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 15
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement: Start with the odd-length data $(0,0,1)$. Define two explicit padding rules to length four. Periodic endpoint padding appends the first entry, giving $x_P=(0,0,1,0)$. Symmetric endpoint padding repeats the final entry, giving $x_S=(0,0,1,1)$. Applying the first Haar stage to the last pair gives $(a,d)=(1/\sqrt2,1/\sqrt2)$ for $x_P$ and $(a,d)=(\sqrt2,0)$ for $x_S$. The coefficients change because the boundary rule changes the pair presented to the filter.

items.title: Exact two-coefficient Haar compression of a four-entry step vector

references.title: Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handouts 3 and 15
Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9

items.statement: For the four-entry step vector $x=(1,1,0,0)$, the finite periodic Haar transform has coefficient vector $(1,1,0,0)$ in the order “coarse average, coarsest detail, finest details.” Retaining the first two coefficients reconstructs $x$ exactly. Among one-coefficient approximations the squared error is $1$.

items.title: Soft thresholding shrinks a retained coefficient while hard best-m retention does not

references.title: Stéphane Mallat, A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Chapter 9
Gilbert Strang and Kevin Amaratunga, Wavelets and Filter Banks, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.327, Handout 15

items.statement: In the standard orthonormal basis, let $c=(3,1)$, choose $m=1$, and use soft threshold $\lambda=1$. Hard best-1 retention gives $(3,0)$ and error norm $1$. Soft thresholding gives $(2,0)$ and error norm $\sqrt2$: it both shrinks the retained coefficient and discards the smaller one.
